decriminalization.summary: Decriminalised in stages: England and Wales in 1967, Scotland in 1980, Northern Ireland in 1982. The age of consent is now 16 for everyone.

marriage.summary: Civil marriage is open to same-sex couples across the UK: England and Wales since 2013, Scotland since 2014, Northern Ireland since 2020. Religious bodies can refuse to conduct same-sex marriages.

sources.label: Marriage (Same-sex Couples) and Civil Partnership (Opposite-sex Couples) (Northern Ireland) Regulations 2019

genderRecognition.summary: A gender recognition certificate requires an application to the Gender Recognition Panel with medical evidence — a diagnosis of gender dysphoria and reports from two doctors — plus, normally, two years living in the acquired gender. Scotland's 2022 self-ID law was blocked by the UK government before it could take effect.

sources.label: Gender Recognition Reform (Scotland) Bill (Prohibition on Submission for Royal Assent) Order 2023

conversionTherapy.summary: No ban is in force. A draft Conversion Practices Bill covering England and Wales was published in June 2026 and is still in pre-legislative scrutiny — it is not law.

asylum.summary: Claims can be based on sexual orientation or gender identity as membership of a particular social group. The 2006 Qualification Regulations set out the refugee definition applied in UK law.

sources.label: Refugee or Person in Need of International Protection (Qualification) Regulations 2006
